question.text: Per SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF6/CIR/P/2020/24 (Feb 6, 2020) and the operational guidelines in Box 10.5, which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the performance benchmarking of AIFs?

answer.text: Performance benchmarking is done on a half-yearly basis using data as on September 30 and March 31 of each year.
AIFs / Schemes that have completed at least ONE year from First Close shall provide the required data to benchmarking agencies.
Data for March 31 must be audited; data for September 30 may be unaudited. Benchmarks shall be reported in BOTH INR and USD.
Performance reporting and benchmarking shall be carried out on POST-TAX Net Asset Value, and AUM shall be the gross commitment including uncalled capital.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Box 10.5 (g) and (f), reporting is on PRE-tax NAV, not post-tax. Per (f), AUM for benchmarking = value of total capital DRAWN DOWN under the Scheme (NOT uncalled commitment). The other three options are accurate: (a) half-yearly reporting; (b) 1-year-from-First-Close threshold; (e) Mar-31 audited vs Sep-30 unaudited; (l) INR + USD dual reporting. **The Trap:** The distractor pairs two independently wrong items (post-tax NAV + gross commitment AUM). Option C bundles multiple true items which may feel 'too detailed to be right' — but it IS correct. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B tests the existence of the framework only. XIX-C tests operational specifics — date conventions, audit requirements, NAV basis, dual-currency reporting. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Lock the drawn-down AUM basis into your Benchmarking Agency data template from day one. A Fund-of-Funds LP doing due diligence will reconcile your reported AUM with the CRISIL/NSE benchmark database — mismatches trigger 'data quality' markdowns in their ODD score.
